texts.error.bad_music: The music setting is %1. It is roland, fm or speaker.
texts.error.bad_version: The version setting is %1. It is 1.1, 1.0 or ir.
texts.error.needs_file: Prince of Persia 2 needs %1. Add it as the project's firmware.
texts.error.needs_file_mt32: Prince of Persia 2 needs %1 for the Roland MT-32's music. Add it as the project's firmware.
texts.error.no_player_name: The Player Name (Hall of Fame) setting has nothing the game can show. Give it a name.
texts.error.no_sounds: SDLPoP2 could not load the sound files.
texts.error.not_loaded: SDLPoP2 could not load the game.
texts.error.out_of_range: The setting %1 is %2. It goes from %3 to %4.
texts.error.preset40: SDLPoP2 did not take PRESET40.DEF as the MT-32's timbres.
texts.error.settings_refused:
SDLPoP2 did not take the project's settings:
%1
texts.firmware.mt32.about: %1 is not one of the game's files. It is %2. You have to supply it when the music is played by the Roland MT-32. The package contains no ROM. Another MT-32 ROM that Munt (the MT-32 emulator used here) knows can be used instead, and the project records exactly which file it was.
texts.firmware.no_data: The package contains none of the game's data. A modified file of your own can be used instead, and the project records exactly which file it was.
texts.firmware.supply_mt32: You have to supply it when the music is played by the Roland MT-32.
texts.firmware.uncracked: The file expected here is the program without a crack. A cracked copy plays the same, because only the copy protection's code differs and SDLPoP2 does not run that code.
texts.firmware.what.caverns_dat: the walls and floors of the caverns
texts.firmware.what.desert_dat: the walls and floors of the desert level
texts.firmware.what.digisnd_dat: the digitized sounds for the Sound Blaster
texts.firmware.what.final_dat: the walls and floors of the final level
texts.firmware.what.ibmsnd_dat: the sounds for the PC speaker
texts.firmware.what.mt32_control_rom: the control ROM of the Roland MT-32, version 1.07, copied from a first-generation unit
texts.firmware.what.mt32_pcm_rom: the PCM ROM of the Roland MT-32, which is the same in every MT-32
texts.firmware.what.nis3vc_dat: the pictures of the story scenes
texts.firmware.what.nisdigi_dat: the digitized sounds of the story scenes
texts.firmware.what.nisibm_dat: the PC speaker sounds of the story scenes
texts.firmware.what.nismidi_dat: the FM music of the story scenes
texts.firmware.what.preset40_def: the instrument sounds (timbres) for the Roland MT-32. It is a piece of MIDI data that the game sends to the MT-32 when it starts, and the game waits until that is done. The DOS setup program copies it to PRESETS.DEF for that device, and on the CD and the install disks it is SNDDRVRS\PRESET40.DEF
texts.firmware.what.presets_def: the FM instruments. The DOS setup program copies the Sound Blaster Pro's instruments to this file, and on the install disks it is SNDDRVRS\PRESET33.DEF. It is needed whatever plays the music, because the timing of the story scenes comes from the FM driver
texts.firmware.what.prince_dat: the pictures and texts that all levels share, the levels themselves and the palettes
texts.firmware.what.prince_exe: the program. SDLPoP2 reads its tables (the characters' animations, how the rooms are drawn and the text)
texts.firmware.what.rooftops_dat: the walls and floors of the rooftop levels
texts.firmware.what.ruins_dat: the walls and floors of the ruins
texts.firmware.what.temple_dat: the walls and floors of the temple
texts.property.alive: Below 0 while alive; counts up once dying
texts.property.frame_delay: 1/60 s between this tick and the next (5 walking, 6 fighting)
texts.property.hp_delta: A pending change of hit points
texts.property.igt_before_clock: Ticks of play from the start of level 1 before the game's clock started, counted as the clock counts (while the prince lives); added to the in-game time with IGT From Level 1
texts.property.igt_ms: The in-game time in milliseconds, 12 ticks a second: IGT mm:ss.mmm
texts.property.igt_ticks: The in-game time: the ticks the game's clock has counted down since the game started (it runs from the first story scene after level 4), and with IGT From Level 1 the ticks of play before that (IGT Before Clock)
texts.property.level_2: Row by row, 10 to a row
texts.property.level_3: How many characters the room starts with
texts.property.max_hp: The hit points a full potion gives back to
texts.property.next_level: The level the game goes to: the level ends when this is not the level being played (15 after level 14: the game is won)
texts.property.ticks_left: Game ticks left of the current minute (719 a minute)
texts.property.x: Across the screen, in the game's units
texts.property.y: Down the screen, in the game's units
texts.setting.base_speed.about: The time between two ticks of play when not fighting, in 1/60 of a second. Smaller is faster. The original has 5.
texts.setting.cheats.about: Starts the program with the cheat word on its command line (yippeeyahoo, or makinit for the initial release), as the original allowed. The cheat buttons exist only when this is on. They cover the DOS game's cheats and SDLPoP2's own. Next Level (Alt+N) can then reach any level.
texts.setting.enable_intro.about: Shows the intro, which is story scenes 7, 4 and 8 of the title sequence. Without it the title goes on to the credits and the demos, where a key starts the game.
texts.setting.enable_story_scenes.about: Shows the story scenes between the levels, the scene when the time runs out and the ending. A skipped scene counts as played to its end, so the game after it is the same.
texts.setting.fight_speed.about: The time between two ticks of play with the sword drawn, in 1/60 of a second. Smaller is faster. The original has 6.
texts.setting.first_level.about: The level a new game starts at. The original starts at 1.
texts.setting.igt_from_level_1.about: Makes the in-game time (IGT, the project's GameTime) count from the very beginning of level 1. The game's own clock stays stopped until the first story scene after level 4, so without this setting the levels before it add nothing. With it, their ticks of play are added, counted the way the clock counts them (while the prince is alive). It changes nothing in the game.
texts.setting.max_hitp_allowed.about: The most hit points the prince can have. Potions of life add nothing above this. The original has 12.
texts.setting.music.about: What plays the sound. 'roland' (the default) plays the music on a Roland MT-32 connected to an MPU-401, which the game's setup program calls "Roland MT-32/LAPC-1/CM-32L". 'fm' plays it on the FM chip of the Sound Blaster Pro, which is what the original setup program chose. Both use the Sound Blaster's digitized sounds. 'speaker' uses the PC speaker alone, with the game's own speaker player and speaker sounds (IBMSND.DAT, NISIBM.DAT). The game knows which device it has. With the speaker it answers "Music Unavailable", plays no background music, and waits after a death or at the end of a level for as long as the speaker's sounds last, as the original did on such a machine. The timing of the story scenes is still the sound card's. The MT-32 needs the setup program's PRESET40.DEF and the two ROMs of an MT-32 (version 1.07), which the project supplies as firmware. With it the game starts 9.35 seconds later, as the original did, while the instrument sounds are sent to the MT-32. So a movie plays back only with the sound device it was made with.
texts.setting.player_name.about: The name that a won game enters in the hall of fame when its time earns a place there. The game types it into its own name editor, as the keys would have typed it. Only the characters in the game's font are used, and only as many as fit in the box (24 at most). The controls have no letter keys, so the game enters the name by itself.
texts.setting.random_seed.about: The starting value (seed) of the game's random number generator. The DOS program took it from the clock. A movie records the number it ran with.
texts.setting.skip_level_reduced_minutes.about: The minutes left after skipping a level with Alt+N when the cheats are off (allowed up to level 3). The original has 15.
texts.setting.skip_title.about: Skips the title sequence. A new game starts immediately, at the level chosen in First level.
texts.setting.start_hitp.about: The prince's hit points when a game starts. The original has 3.
texts.setting.start_minutes_left.about: The minutes left when a game starts. The original has 75.
texts.setting.ticks_per_minute.about: How many ticks of the game clock make one minute of the time left. The original has 719. A tick is 1/12 of a second, so a minute of the clock lasts 59.92 seconds.
texts.setting.version.about: Which DOS release of the game is played. The project supplies that release's files (see SDLPoP2's docs/VERSIONS.md). '1.1' is the release on the Prince of Persia Collection CD, which SDLPoP2 is rebuilt from. The others are '1.0' and the initial release ('ir'). The releases differ in movement near walls and gates, the guards, the spirit, levels 2, 5, 8 and 14, the timers and random numbers, and a few story scenes. 1.0 and 1.1 have the same data files and differ only in PRINCE.EXE. The initial release has files of its own (twelve of them differ), and its cheat word is makinit.
